title: Why a Third-of-a-Pound Animal Stacks 60 Pounds of Hay
subject: pika

scenes.text: Why does an animal that weighs a third of a pound stack up 60 pounds of hay?
It's the American pika, a tiny mountain animal, and it never hibernates.
All summer it runs back and forth, collecting grasses and wildflowers.
It dries them in the sun, then hauls the hay into a den among the rocks.
Then snow buries the mountain, and the pika eats from its pile all winter, moving through snow tunnels.
The twist: pikas can overheat at around 78 degrees Fahrenheit, so a hot summer means less time to stack hay.

description:
A pika weighs about a third of a pound, yet it collects around 60 pounds of hay to survive winter.
It never hibernates, so that haystack is its whole winter menu.
Could you survive on a pile you stacked yourself?
first_comment: Pikas overheat at about 78 degrees Fahrenheit. Would you rather stack hay or hibernate?
